stem: For which comparison is the t-test the appropriate statistical test?

options.content: The mean lengths of leaves from two different sites
options.rationale: Correct: two means of continuous data.

options.content: Numbers of offspring in four phenotype classes against a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio
options.rationale: Counts in categories against expected numbers need chi-squared.

options.content: Whether light intensity is related to the number of plant species in quadrats
options.rationale: A relationship between two variables needs a correlation test.

options.content: The diversity of insect species in a sample from one field
options.rationale: Diversity is measured with Simpson's index.

explanation: The t-test compares the means of two samples of continuous data.

stem: Which is the null hypothesis for a t-test comparing the masses of seeds from irrigated and unirrigated plots?

options.content: There is no significant difference between the mean seed masses of the two plots
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Seeds from the irrigated plot are significantly heavier than seeds from the other plot
options.rationale: This is an alternative hypothesis.

options.content: Irrigation causes an increase in the mean mass of the seeds produced
options.rationale: A null hypothesis states no difference, and tests do not show cause.

options.content: The seed masses in each plot follow a normal distribution
options.rationale: This is an assumption of the test, not its null hypothesis.

explanation: Null hypothesis: no significant difference between the means; any difference is due to chance.

stem: A t-test gives t = 1.46. The critical value at p = 0.05 is 2.12. What should be concluded?

options.content: The difference is significant; reject the null hypothesis
options.rationale: That needs t greater than 2.12.

options.content: The difference is not significant; accept the null hypothesis
options.rationale: Correct: t is below the critical value.

options.content: The two samples have been shown to have identical means
options.rationale: Accepting the null hypothesis does not show the means are equal.

options.content: The test is invalid because t is smaller than 2
options.rationale: Any positive value of t is valid.

explanation: 1.46 < 2.12, so the difference is not significant and is due to chance; accept the null hypothesis.

stem: Two pairs of samples have the same difference between their means. In the first pair the standard deviations are much larger. How will t compare?

options.content: t will be larger for the first pair
options.rationale: Greater variability reduces t.

options.content: t will be the same, because the means differ equally
options.rationale: t depends on the spread as well as the difference.

options.content: t will be smaller for the first pair
options.rationale: Correct: larger s gives a larger denominator.

options.content: t cannot be calculated when the standard deviations are large
options.rationale: It can; it will simply be small.

explanation: t = difference ÷ √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂); larger standard deviations increase the denominator and reduce t.
hints: Where does s appear in the formula?

stem: Which condition is an assumption of the t-test?

options.content: Every expected value in each category is at least 5
options.rationale: This applies to the chi-squared test.

options.content: Both samples must contain more than 30 values
options.rationale: The t-test is designed for small samples.

options.content: Data in each sample are approximately normally distributed
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The two variables must have been measured on each individual
options.rationale: That describes paired data for correlation.

explanation: The t-test assumes continuous, roughly normally distributed data with similar standard deviations.
hints: Think about the shape of the distribution.

stem: A student finds t = 3.40 with 10 values in each sample. Critical values: 2.10 at p = 0.05 and 2.88 at p = 0.01 (18 degrees of freedom). Which statement is correct?

options.content: The difference is significant at p = 0.05 but not at p = 0.01
options.rationale: t (3.40) is also above 2.88.

options.content: The degrees of freedom should be 9, so the critical values are wrong
There is a 3.40% chance that the null hypothesis is true
options.rationale: t is not a probability.

options.content: The probability that the difference is due to chance is less than 1%
options.rationale: Correct: t exceeds even the p = 0.01 value.

explanation: 3.40 > 2.88, so p < 0.01: the difference is highly significant.
hints: Compare t with both critical values.

stem: Students compared the heights of maize plants grown with and without manure, using 5 plants per treatment, and found t below the critical value. What is the best next step?

options.content: Conclude that manure has no effect on the growth of maize plants of any variety
options.rationale: A non-significant result with tiny samples is weak evidence of no effect.

options.content: Repeat with many more plants, because small samples make real differences hard to detect
options.rationale: Correct: larger n reduces the standard errors and increases t if the difference is real.

options.content: Use the chi-squared test instead, as it is more sensitive
options.rationale: Chi-squared is for counts in categories, not heights.

options.content: Remove the tallest unmanured plant so that the means differ more
options.rationale: Removing data to get a result is not valid.

explanation: With n = 5 the standard errors are large; a bigger sample gives the test more power to detect a real difference.
hints: What does n do to the denominator of t?

stem: A t-test compares 11 leaves from one tree with 13 leaves from another. How many degrees of freedom are used?

The tail lengths of 12 mice from a grassland site had a mean of 34.2 mm (s = 4.1 mm); 12 mice from a woodland site had a mean of 29.8 mm (s = 3.6 mm). Using $t = \dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\sqrt{\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2}}}$, calculate t to three significant figures.
explanation:
1. $\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} = \dfrac{4.1^2}{12} = 1.4008$ and $\dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2} = \dfrac{3.6^2}{12} = 1.0800$.
2. $\sqrt{2.4808} = 1.5751$.
3. $t = \dfrac{34.2 - 29.8}{1.5751} = 2.79$.
With 22 degrees of freedom the critical value is 2.07, so the difference is significant. Forgetting to square s gives 5.49.
workedSolution:
1. $\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} = \dfrac{4.1^2}{12} = 1.4008$ and $\dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2} = \dfrac{3.6^2}{12} = 1.0800$.
2. $\sqrt{2.4808} = 1.5751$.
3. $t = \dfrac{34.2 - 29.8}{1.5751} = 2.79$.
With 22 degrees of freedom the critical value is 2.07, so the difference is significant. Forgetting to square s gives 5.49.
hints: Square each standard deviation before dividing by n.

stem: Rudo measured the heights (cm) of six hybrid maize plants (182, 195, 176, 201, 188, 190) and six open-pollinated plants (165, 178, 160, 172, 181, 168) of the same age. Using $s = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}}$ and $t = \dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\sqrt{\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2}}}$, calculate t to three significant figures.
explanation:
1. Means: hybrid $= 1132 \div 6 = 188.67$ cm; open-pollinated $= 1024 \div 6 = 170.67$ cm.
2. Standard deviations (dividing by 5): $s_1 = 8.937$ cm; $s_2 = 7.941$ cm.
3. $\dfrac{s_1^2}{6} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{6} = 13.311 + 10.511 = 23.822$; square root $= 4.881$.
4. $t = 18.00 \div 4.881 = 3.69$.
With 10 degrees of freedom the critical value is 2.23: the difference is significant.
workedSolution:
1. Means: hybrid $= 1132 \div 6 = 188.67$ cm; open-pollinated $= 1024 \div 6 = 170.67$ cm.
2. Standard deviations (dividing by 5): $s_1 = 8.937$ cm; $s_2 = 7.941$ cm.
3. $\dfrac{s_1^2}{6} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{6} = 13.311 + 10.511 = 23.822$; square root $= 4.881$.
4. $t = 18.00 \div 4.881 = 3.69$.
With 10 degrees of freedom the critical value is 2.23: the difference is significant.
hints: Find both means and both standard deviations first.

stem: A larger difference between the two sample means, with everything else unchanged, gives a larger value of t.
explanation: True. The difference between the means is the numerator of t.

stem: If t is greater than the critical value, the difference between the means is due to chance.
explanation: False. t above the critical value means the difference is significant: unlikely to be due to chance; reject the null hypothesis.

stem: Match each investigation with the most appropriate statistical test.

left.content: Mean wing length of mosquitoes from two villages
Numbers of red, roan and white calves against a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio
Whether soil pH is linearly related to plant height, data normally distributed
Whether distance from a path is related to the abundance rank of a weed

explanation: Two means: t-test; counts against a ratio: χ²; linear relationship with normal data: Pearson; ranked or non-normal data: Spearman.
hints: Is the question about a difference, a fit to a ratio, or a relationship?

stem: Complete the sentence.

payload.template: For a t-test on two samples of 9 and 7 values, the degrees of freedom are {{blank:a}}, and the test assumes that the data are {{blank:b}} distributed.

explanation: 9 + 7 − 2 = 14; data approximately normally distributed.

stem: Name the statistical test used to find whether the means of two samples of continuous data differ significantly.
explanation: The t-test.

stem: Explain why the t-test is suitable for comparing the masses of hens' eggs from two farms, and why chi-squared would not be.

points.description: Two samples / two means are being compared
Mass is continuous data, likely normally distributed with similar spread
Chi-squared needs counts in categories compared with expected numbers, which these data are not

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The investigation compares the means of two samples, and egg mass is a continuous measurement that is likely to be roughly normally distributed with similar spread on both farms, so the t-test fits. Chi-squared compares observed counts in categories with expected counts from a hypothesis, so it cannot be used on masses.

explanation: Match the test to the data type and question.
hints: What kind of data does each test need?

stem: In a t-test comparing the lengths of bean seeds from two varieties, t = 4.62 with 20 degrees of freedom (critical value at p = 0.05 is 2.09). Write a full conclusion.

points.description: 4.62 is greater than the critical value of 2.09 (20 df, p = 0.05)
So the difference between the means is significant / unlikely to be due to chance (p < 0.05)
Reject the null hypothesis: the two varieties differ in mean seed length

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The calculated t of 4.62 is greater than the critical value of 2.09 for 20 degrees of freedom at p = 0.05. The probability that the difference is due to chance is less than 5%, so it is significant. The null hypothesis is rejected: the mean seed lengths of the two varieties are significantly different.

explanation: Compare, state significance, decide on the null hypothesis.

stem: A t-test shows that sorghum plants on one farm are significantly taller than on a neighbouring farm. The farmer concludes that his new fertiliser caused the difference. Evaluate this conclusion.

points.description: The test shows only that the means differ significantly, not what caused the difference
Other variables may differ between farms: soil type, water / rainfall, variety, planting date, pests
A controlled trial on one farm with randomly assigned fertilised and unfertilised plots (with replicates) is needed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The t-test only shows that the difference in mean height is unlikely to be due to chance; it says nothing about the cause. The farms may differ in soil, water supply, variety, planting date or pests, any of which could explain the difference. To test the fertiliser, plots on the same farm should be randomly assigned to fertilised and unfertilised treatments, with replicates.

explanation: Significance is not causation.

stem:
Chipo measured the lengths of eight mosquito larvae from each of two breeding pools in the Zambezi valley.

| Pool | Lengths of larvae / mm |
|---|---|
| Pool 1 | 7.2, 6.8, 7.9, 7.5, 6.6, 7.1, 7.7, 7.0 |
| Pool 2 | 6.1, 6.6, 5.8, 6.4, 6.9, 6.0, 6.3, 5.9 |

For pool 2, the mean is 6.250 mm and the standard deviation is 0.374 mm. The formulae are $s = \sqrt{\dfrac{\sum (x - \bar{x})^2}{n - 1}}$ and $t = \dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\sqrt{\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2}}}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: State a null hypothesis for this investigation.

points.description: There is no significant difference between the mean lengths of larvae in the two pools; any difference is due to chance

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There is no significant difference between the mean larval lengths in the two pools; any difference is due to chance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give two reasons why a t-test is appropriate.

points.description: Comparing the means of two (independent) samples
Length is continuous data, approximately normally distributed / similar standard deviations

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The means of two independent samples are being compared, and length is continuous data that is likely to be roughly normally distributed with similar spread in both pools.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the mean length for pool 1, in mm, to three decimal places.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Σ(x − x̄)² for pool 1 is 1.395 mm². Calculate the standard deviation for pool 1, in mm, to three decimal places.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Calculate t, to three significant figures.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: State the number of degrees of freedom.

parts.label: (g)
parts.stem: The critical value at p = 0.05 is 2.14. State your conclusion.

points.description: t (4.73) is greater than 2.14, so the difference is significant / not due to chance
Reject the null hypothesis: larvae in pool 1 are significantly longer

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: t = 4.73 is greater than the critical value of 2.14, so the difference is significant and the null hypothesis is rejected: larvae in pool 1 are significantly longer.

parts.label: (h)
parts.stem: Suggest one variable that might explain the difference between the pools.

points.description: Water temperature, food supply / organic matter, larval age or density, predators, species of mosquito (any one)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The larvae in pool 1 may be older, or the water may be warmer or richer in food.

explanation: Null hypothesis, justify the test, mean, SD, t, df and conclude.

stem:
Tatenda tested extracts of two plants for antibacterial activity. Seven paper discs soaked in each extract were placed on agar plates seeded with bacteria, and the diameter of the clear zone around each disc was measured.

| Extract | Mean diameter / mm | Standard deviation / mm | Number of discs |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 14.3 | 1.9 | 7 |
| B | 12.6 | 2.2 | 7 |

The formula is $t = \dfrac{|\bar{x}_1 - \bar{x}_2|}{\sqrt{\dfrac{s_1^2}{n_1} + \dfrac{s_2^2}{n_2}}}$.

points.description: No significant difference between the mean diameters of the clear zones for extracts A and B

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: There is no significant difference between the mean zone diameters for extracts A and B; any difference is due to chance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate t, to three significant figures.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The critical value at p = 0.05 is 2.18. What can Tatenda conclude?

points.description: t (1.55) is less than 2.18, so the difference is not significant / due to chance
Accept the null hypothesis: no evidence that extract A is more effective

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: t = 1.55 is less than 2.18, so the difference is not significant and is likely to be due to chance. The null hypothesis is accepted: there is no evidence that extract A is more effective than B.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Suggest two changes that would make the comparison more reliable.

points.description: Use more discs / replicate plates (larger n reduces the standard errors)
Standardise extract concentration, disc size, volume absorbed, incubation time and temperature / use the same bacterial lawn density

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Use more discs on more plates, so the standard errors are smaller. Make sure the extracts are at the same concentration and that disc size, volume absorbed, incubation temperature and time and the density of bacteria are kept the same.

explanation: A non-significant t: accept the null hypothesis and suggest ways to reduce variability or increase n.
hints: Square each standard deviation and divide by 7.
